questions.question: Name the seven continents and five oceans, and explain why Africa may look smaller than it really is on a flat world map.
questions.expected_answer: Continents: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia (Oceania), Antarctica. Oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic. A flat map cannot show a round Earth without distortion; many world maps stretch places far from the equator, so countries such as Greenland look much bigger than they are while Africa, which lies across the equator, looks relatively small.

questions.question: Describe the location of a place in the news on three levels, using Nairobi as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Continent and ocean: Nairobi is in East Africa, inland from the Indian Ocean. Country and neighbours: it is the capital of Kenya, which borders Tanzania, Uganda, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan. Degrees: about 1 degree S, 37 degrees E, almost on the equator.

questions.question: Explain two ways of finding north without a compass in South Africa, and why compass directions are better than left and right on a sketch map.
questions.expected_answer: In the morning, point your right arm at the rising sun (east) and you face roughly north. At midday your shadow points roughly south because the sun is in the northern sky, so north is the opposite way. Compass directions stay the same whichever way a person faces, while left and right change with the direction you face.
